exposure: High-flow continuous positive airway pressure (20l/min >= 15 PEEP) in the delivery room
cohort: Infants born below 30 gestational weeks, divided into a treatment group receiving a standardized early respiratory management protocol (n=37) and a control group receiving standard respiratory support (n=46).
finding: The study found that a standardized early respiratory management protocol for premature infants led to a shorter duration of mechanical ventilation, oxygen therapy, and hospital stay, as well as a lower frequency of severe chronic complications like bronchopulmonary dysplasia and intraventricular hemorrhages.
